lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Options for a project folder: $2 card folder or $8 plastic folder. Criteria: keep pages dry, spend under $5. Which choice fits both criteria, or which criterion must you drop?

FEEDBACK
The $2 folder fits the budget but may fail “dry” in rain. The $8 folder fails “under $5” because $8 > $5. You cannot meet both unless you change a criterion. A honest record says which criterion you rank first.

WATCH FOR
Writing the choice with no options and no criterion. A record can be checked by someone else only if the reason is visible.

WORKED MODEL
Options: walk (free, 35 minutes) or bus ($4, 15 minutes). Criteria: arrive on time, spend little. If the bell is in 20 minutes, the bus wins on time and the opportunity cost is the $4. If you have 40 minutes, walking wins on cost. The record states the situation first.

TRY FIRST
Options for a project folder: $2 card folder or $8 plastic folder. Criteria: keep pages dry, spend under $5. Which choice fits both criteria, or which criterion must you drop?

FEEDBACK
The $2 folder fits the budget but may fail “dry” in rain. The $8 folder fails “under $5” because $8 > $5. You cannot meet both unless you change a criterion. A honest record says which criterion you rank first.
teach_steps.explain:
A decision record makes a choice inspectable. It lists the options, the criteria, the choice, and the reason linked to a criterion. “I just wanted it” is a feeling, not a finished record. The reason should name which criterion won. If two criteria conflict, the record says which one you ranked higher and what you gave up.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
